note: The tr.wikipedia list article dates this accident 23 October 2024. Contemporary reporting places it, with the same toll and the same make-up of the dead, at Eti Bakır's Madenköy site on 23 November 2023, which is what the register publishes after reviewer decisions 283-285. The source statement stands superseded, not unexamined.

The dedicated article narrates 13 rising to 14; the register publishes 17. Both are right at their own dates. The Chamber of Mining Engineers' statement at the time gives 13 deaths with six people seriously injured, and its 2010-2020 accident report gives 17. The toll was revised upward over time, so the record carries casualty_status 'revised' with both observations dated, and the source statement of 13 stands as the first observation, not as a dispute.

Wikidata states 66 deaths. The Chamber of Mining Engineers' statement of 7 February 2023 commemorates 68, which the register publishes and now cites. The Wikidata figure stays on file as a claim that was not selected.

The list entry describes two accidents of the same day in one sentence: two deaths at Amasra and one at Gelik. Read mechanically, the second toll attaches to the first place, which is where the stated 1 comes from. A local report of the day records the second recovery at 13:35. The register publishes 2 at Amasra and 1 at Gelik as separate records.
